title: Trace adapter and microburst synthesizer: low-overhead trace hooks + hybrid burn-rate heuristics
creator: Alex Chen
description:
Goal: Improve detection and alerting for short-duration high-latency/error microbursts without generating noisy pages. Deliver a lightweight trace-hook adapter that tags requests with route-level latency signatures and a microburst synthesizer in the metrics pipeline that produces an anomaly confidence score used by tiered burn-rate alerts and paging policies.

Scope:
- Trace adapter (low overhead): sampling-friendly hook implemented as an extensible middleware for runtime agents. Adds deterministic route and sequence fingerprints and a small set of latency/error histograms to spans.
- Metrics/log pipeline enrichment: histogram-to-timeseries smoothing, burst-window delta counters, and span-weighted error attribution to compute a per-route microburst_score/time_bucket.
- Alerting/Runbooks: a hybrid burn-rate heuristic combining classic error-budget burn with microburst_score to delay or escalate paging depending on confidence and customer impact. New anomaly_score field is propagated to alert rules.
- Dashboards: microburst heatmap (time x route), per-tenant error fingerprinting, and a burn-rate confidence panel for oncall.

Non-goals: large-scale sampling changes, full AIOps automation, or replacing existing SLO definitions. This is an incremental capability to reduce noisy pages for transient spikes while surfacing impactful regressions faster.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Trace adapter instrumentation adds <=1% p50 latency overhead on common request paths in load tests.
2) Microburst synthesizer emits a time-series microburst_score with documented query examples and unit tests.
3) Burn-rate alerting rules updated to reference microburst_score and have test harness that simulates microbursts to validate non-paging vs paging outcomes.
4) New dashboard panels deployed to Canaries and accessible from Console group 'Observability -> Microbursts'.
5) Playbook updated with tiered paging decision matrix and sample PagerDuty flows.

Implementation notes:
- Adapter implemented as a small shim in runtime agents (C++) and a Node/Python middleware for edge services; config flag for 'microburst_tags' to enable per-deployment.
- Pipeline enrichment runs as a lightweight stream transformation (Kafka Streams / Flink job prototype). We will initially implement as a consumer transformer in the observability ingestion service to iterate faster, then move to dedicated stream job if needed.
- Microburst window defaults: 10s roll with 3-s sampling buckets; anomaly scoring uses histogram tail-percentile delta and a weighted error rate. Tunables surfaced in Console.
- Alerting: add rule variants: (a) low-confidence burn-rate (no page, slack alert), (b) medium-confidence (notify SRE channel), (c) high-confidence (page oncall). Confidence thresholds and business impact will be combined by a simple rule matrix.

Rollout plan:
1) Developer preview in Canary runtime (feature flag), observe ingestion and compute cost.
2) Beta with selected tenant groups (customer-impact medium) and guardrail config.
3) GA rollout with default off and recommended policy templates.

Related artifacts: Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Microburst+Detection+Spec (draft), GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/4217 (WIP), Dashboard mock: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/microburst-heatmap-v1.png
